Stated Claim / Post Context:
Dramatic escalation in Milky Lane co-founder Pete Haselhurst's extortion case: Members locked out after he abruptly shuts down CHANGE gym and sends extraordinary email - as police track down alleged 'debt collectors'

Locked doors. A bizarre explanation. As police extradite alleged 'debt collectors' linked to the extortion case, questions are swirling around Pete Haselhurst's abruptly shuttered CHANGE gym.

Actual Article Body:
By CANDACE SUTTON, SENIOR NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  22:35 AEDT, 22 October 2026   |  Updated:  22:36 AEDT, 22 October 2026

CHANGE Fitness boss and Milky Lane co-founder Pete Haselhurst has abruptly shut down a major Gold Coast gym while on bail for extortion, stalking and drug charges.

It follows the extradition of three mysterious 'debt collectors of Middle Eastern appearance from Sydney', who allegedly made threats and demanded money from individuals who held franchises in CHANGE and Haselhurst's former hamburger chain. They were brought from NSW to Queensland on Thursday afternoon to face multiple extortion charges.

The previous Thursday, staff at the Broadbeach CHANGE gym arrived at work to find themselves locked out and classes cancelled, after Haselhurst and his wife, Emma Jean Pearson, unexpectedly closed the business.

Rumours are now circulating in Gold Coast gym circles that the landlord forced them to close due to unpaid rent.

Haselhurst was released from prison only last month after spending six weeks behind bars following his July arrest for allegedly extorting former business partners with the help of men 'known to NSW police'.

Queensland Police confirmed three men, aged 35, 38 and 45, were being extradited to the Gold Coast.

All are scheduled to appear at Southport Magistrates Court on Friday, facing multiple charges of extortion with intent to gain benefit through threats of detriment.

This follows alleged incidents at Mermaid Waters and Currumbin Waters, where unknown men identified themselves as 'debt collectors' and demanded a significant amount of money from former business associates.

CHANGE Fitness boss and Milky Lane co-founder Pete Haselhurst (pictured with his wife and business partner, Emma Jean Pearson) has abruptly shut down a major Gold Coast gym while on bail for extortion, stalking and drug charges

Staff arrived last Thursday to find themselves locked out, classes cancelled, and rumours swirling that the landlord had shut the gym due to unpaid rent - but Haselhurst insists it's a new beginning

Haselhurst is facing eight charges including three counts of extortion and three of unlawful stalking, and one count of possessing dangerous drugs. Ms Pearson is not implicated

These included allegedly terrorising Haselhurst's former partners in the cult burger chain, Milky Lane.

The Daily Mail has sought responses from Queensland Police regarding the extraditions. Meanwhile, Haselhurst and Pearson have moved to calm the uproar over the Broadbeach gym closure.

On Facebook, one client posted sarcastically: 'So kind of Change Broadbeach to cancel classes... have the doors locked and ZERO communication even when emailed AND messaged on Instagram, with its members happy to charge us our weekly fee last week. SHAME ON YOU.'

One instructor responded, saying the owners 'have been nothing short of supportive, communicating and explaining to members', while Haselhurst and Pearson sent an email claiming the closure was 'an eleventh hour' decision.

'We were presented with an unexpected opportunity that we felt we could not pass up,' they said.

The email stated that the gym would be taken over by Brisbane fitness entrepreneurs Emil Juresic and Giselle Kramer, whose Level X 'state-of-the-art gym and luxury wellness empire' is expanding to the Gold Coast in December.

Haselhurst and Pearson have moved to calm the uproar over the Broadbeach gym closure

On Facebook, one client posted a sarcastic, 'so kind of Change Broadbeach to cancel classes... have the doors locked and ZERO communication even when emailed AND messaged on Instagram ... SHAME ON YOU'

While Level X confirmed to the Mail it would be 'taking over the space' at the CHANGE gym premises, fitness contractors have expressed concern about being paid during the month-long renovation.

The email reassured CHANGE members: 'Emma and I will be there, training alongside you. While the transition is emotional for us, we are excited about what it will bring to the community we love.'

Ms Pearson, who previously told the Mail that reports of her partner's arrest 'were incorrect' and later said, 'I'm not interested,' is not implicated in the police charges.

Haselhurst is facing eight charges, including three counts of extortion, three of unlawful stalking, one count of possessing dangerous drugs and one count of possessing prescription medicines or hazardous poisons.

The court heard during one of Haselhurst's bail applications that a couple was confronted at their home in Mermaid Waters at about 10.50am on July 18, with Queensland Police telling the Daily Mail that 'two unknown men identified themselves as "debt collectors", demanded a significant amount of money, and made threats'.

Haselhurst spent six weeks behind bars before being released on bail, after a court heard video of 'debt collectors' berating business associates of the CHANGE founder for money

Haselhurst and Pearson said the closure was 'an eleventh hour' decision, explaining: 'We were presented with an unexpected opportunity we felt we could not pass up'

The 28-year-old man and the 27-year-old woman 'were then transported to a café at a nearby shopping centre.

'[There] they met with a 39-year-old man, who they had previously been involved in a Broadbeach business venture with in 2025. Further threats were allegedly made.'

The court was played a video in which one 'debt collector' repeatedly berated the pair, saying 'Listen here you motherf***er, if you owe this c*** money, you gotta sit with him and sort it out, you understand?'

In another conversation between the complainants and a second debt collector, he said, 'You robbed him a hundred grand, brother.' Both debt collectors were 'physically imposing'.

Then, on a Sunday morning about 8.20am at Currumbin Waters, 'the same two men attended the house of a 47-year-old man... where they demanded a significant amount of money and made threats', police said.

The man reportedly refused to leave the house he shared with his partner and their children, who were not home at the time, as the two men demanded money.

The Mail understands that Haselhurst was building CHANGE as an alternative to the once-ubiquitous F45 fitness empire, having run F45 Bondi Beach for six years before departing in 2020.

Haselhurst parted ways with the Milky Lane burger and milkshake chain he co-founded about the same time he left F45. He has also run franchise businesses called Adventure Tours, Lost Paradise, Lost Picnic and The Entrepreneur Degree.

On its website, CHANGE - now rebranded as Change Life Enhanced - promises 'workouts designed by the world's best to help you unlock your limitless potential'.

In videos promoting his business - which has afforded Haselhurst a luxury jet-set lifestyle - he plugs a new 'House of Health' in Sydney's Surry Hills as a 'one-stop' solution to 'health, performance, and longevity'.

Haselhurst personally ran the Broadbeach gym, as well as a gym in North Adelaide and a proposed forthcoming Surry Hills branch.

However, three Gold Coast franchises at North Lakes, Sunnybank and Coomera have closed.

According to one of his websites, Haselhurst created 'the most successful franchisee in the entire F45 Training network' in Bondi, which 'was crowned the number one F45 studio in the world for eight consecutive years'.
